content_metadata.description: This video explores the fascinating astronomical phenomena of quasars, focusing on their nature, formation, and impact on the universe.

qAndA.answer: The accretion of matter into a supermassive black hole at its center.
qAndA.question: What is the primary source of energy for a quasar?

qAndA.answer: Quasars release powerful jets and radiation that can suppress the formation of new stars within their galaxies.
qAndA.question: What is the "feedback" process associated with quasars?

qAndA.answer: The collision of the Andromeda and Milky Way galaxies, merging their supermassive black holes.
qAndA.question: What event could potentially lead to the formation of a brighter quasar in the future?

qAndA.answer: Radio-loud quasars emit powerful jets, visible as bright streams emanating from their centers, while radio-quiet quasars lack these prominent jets.
qAndA.question: What visual characteristic distinguishes radio-loud quasars from radio-quiet quasars?

qAndA.answer: After consuming the surrounding matter and gas, quasars cool down, their activity diminishes, and they settle into a quieter state resembling a normal galaxy.
qAndA.question: How do quasars eventually transition into normal galaxies?

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: What is a quasar?
Is it a galaxy?
Or is it a black hole?
What if I say it's like a combination of both with some differences?
Let's get to the topic.
quasar is an extreme light emitting active galactic nucleus.
It was called as quasisteller object, there after named as quasar, a compact region
at the center of a galaxy that has a much higher than normal luminosity.
These are known as the most energetic and luminous objects in the universe.
It emits radiation in all directions.
It doesn't only emit radiation, it also gets fueled by the accreted material around
it.
A quasar forms when material falls into the accretion disk around a supermassive black
hole at the center of a galaxy.
quasars show the locations of supermassive black holes which grow by accretion of matter.
The largest known quasar is estimated to consume matter of 10 Earths per second.
Let's discuss main types of quasars.
Radio-loud quasars, these contain powerful jets, only 10% of all quasars known are
radio-loud.
Radio-quiet quasars, these lack-powerful jets, 90% of all quasars known are radio-quiet.
Red quasars are the quasars that are mostly radio-quiet or loud quasars which look red
in color and which doesn't have much luminosity.
Last but not least, micro-quasars are smallest quasars ever known, one of these can light
up our mother Earth completely.
Vars can emit light of a trillion times brighter than the light coming from our sun.
They contain massive black holes and they may represent a stage in the evolution of some
galaxies.
When two quasars collide, it will actually be two supermassive black holes colliding
and result to destruction of the surroundings in form of gravitational wave fluctuations.
It is believed that when Andromeda Galaxy and our own Milky Way Galaxy collide after
four billion years, they might get their cores united and may form a quasar which will
be brighter than many known quasars.
A quasar has black hole that draws in matter from the surrounding space.
After a quasar is done accruing the surrounding gases and matter, it cools down and turns
into a normal galaxy.
It is believed that quasars are powered by accretion.
The accretion disk is combined with gases, matter, nebulae and other materials.
Quasars are destructive, they shut down the formation of stars by a process called feedback,
they release jets, strong radio emission, radiation and energy which is strong enough to wipe
out young stars in their galaxies.
This destruction of quasar is quite helpful for stabilization of universe, this prevented
many star formations and saved the surroundings from supernovae blasts that could cause havoc
in the entire space.
Its strong gravitational field causes it to radiate across a wide range.
Its core temperature may be hotter than 10 trillion degrees.
The brightest quasar in sky is 3C273, it is in the constellation Virgo.
It was found in 1900s by an Australian radio station where they pointed anti-nass for the
first time towards space, at the time they found many strange radio waves, one of these
strange things are quasars.
Many scientists believe that quasars are supermassive black holes with an accretion disk
